newsitem.title: USA: Marine pilot ejects safely onto carrier deck.
newsitem.headline: Marine pilot ejects safely onto carrier deck.

text.p: A Marine Corps pilot ejected and landed safely on the deck of an aircraft carrier after ditching his fighter jet in the Pacific Ocean, officials said Thursday.

The pilot, who was not immediately identified, was practicing night landings in his F/A 18 Hornet aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln when the accident occurred Wednesday night, said James Jackson, senior chief petty officer with the Navy's Pacific fleet command in San Diego.

He said the pilot, based at Miramar Naval Air Station near San Diego, suffered no serious injuries but was being transported to a hospital for observation. Details of the accident off the Washington coast were not immediately available, but the Hornet was lost.
The Abraham Lincoln has been undergoing sea trials ahead of its relocation next month from the naval shipyard in Bremerton to its new home port in Everett, Wash., north of Seattle.
